source_excerpts.text:
The existence-to-construction gap can be closed in an exact linear-optimization oracle model, at the level of a complete candidate proof. The construction replaces nonconvex global minimization with rational local descent, exact transitions to smaller faces, and a bounded-bit precision repair. A finite separation argument then constructs a compact distribution with the prescribed mean.
This remains an unreviewed mathematical derivation, not an independently verified theorem or a completed implementation of the full rounding algorithm.
A provenance correction matters: an earlier Astra manuscript already proposed a constructive \(1161k\) theorem. I recovered and reconstructed that argument rather than treating its conclusion as established. The principal change in this investigation is a simpler precision-repair operation, together with further weighted-edge and integral-base-polyhedron consequences. I am not claiming that the constructive theorem was first discovered in this run.    Pasted text(20261006-162929)
Let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) have Boolean vertices. Suppose every actual edge changes at most \(k\) coordinates, where \(1\le k\le n\) is a supplied upper bound. Let \(x\in P\) and \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\) be rational, with
\[ \max_j\|A_{\cdot j}\|_2\le1. \]
The access assumption is an exact linear-optimization oracle for the original \(P\): given a rational objective, it returns an optimizing Boolean vertex. It is not an oracle for the spectral potential or the unknown set of good vertices.
There is a deterministic, polynomial-bit, oracle-efficient algorithm returning vertices \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\) and rational probabilities \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r\) such that
\[ \boxed{ r\le \dim F(x)+1\le n+1,\qquad \sum_{\ell=1}^r\lambda_\ell v_\ell=x, } \]
and every supported vertex satisfies
\[ \boxed{ \|A(v_\ell-x)\|_\infty<B(k), \qquad B(k)=16\lfloor\sqrt{64k}\rfloor^2+136k+1 \le1161k. } \]
Here \(F(x)\) is the minimal original face containing \(x\). Every output remains in that face.
For any rational linear cost \(c\), the algorithm can instead directly construct a good vertex satisfying
\[ c^\top v\le c^\top x. \]
For a matroid base polytope, an independence oracle suffices. Its edges have support two, giving
\[ \boxed{ \mathbb E\mathbf1_B=x,\qquad \|A(\mathbf1_B-x)\|_\infty<2209 \quad\text{for every supported basis}. } \]

source_excerpts.text:
The replacement repair is elementary but addresses that issue directly.
Suppose a rational candidate \(z\) lies in an original face \(F\), and it satisfies a fixed rational affine constraint
\[ Cy=d. \]
In the rounding algorithm, this is the temporary cost slice \(c^\top y=c^\top x_0\), whose right-hand side comes from the original input.
Choose a dyadic mesh \(h=2^{-p}\) and enclose \(z\) coordinatewise:
\[ \ell_j=h\lfloor z_j/h\rfloor,\qquad I_j=[\ell_j,\ell_j+h]. \]
Now return a vertex of the ordinary rational linear-programming polytope
\[ \boxed{ F\cap\{y:Cy=d\}\cap\prod_j I_j. } \]
This is not a nonconvex optimization problem.
The intersection contains \(z\), so it is nonempty. Its returned point \(\widehat z\) satisfies
\[ \|\widehat z-z\|_\infty\le h, \qquad \|\widehat z-z\|_2\le\sqrt n\,h, \]
while preserving the affine constraint exactly and remaining in \(F\).
A vertex of the intersection is determined by at most \(n\) independent facet, face, slice, and cell equations. Boolean polytopes admit integer facet and affine-hull descriptions with \(O(n\log n)\)-bit coefficients, by determinant bounds. The cell endpoints have \(O(p)\) bits. Therefore Cramer’s rule bounds the output encoding polynomially in the original data and \(p\), independently of the candidate’s denominator length.
Two distinctions are essential.
The returned point need not be dyadic. A slice such as \(y_1=1/3\) may prohibit that. The enclosing cell is dyadic; the returned point is rational.
The cell is discarded after repair. Subsequent directions use the minimal face of the original polytope, not the artificial faces of the clipped cell. The repaired point may enter a smaller original face; that is permitted and useful.
For explicitly listed rational inequalities, I implemented this operation without an LP solver: repeatedly choose a rational direction annihilating the active constraints and push to the first boundary. Each push adds an independent active constraint, so at most \(n\) pushes reach a vertex of the clipped slice. In the general oracle model, ordinary exact rational LP supplies the same operation.
This removes the need for the earlier, more elaborate affine-anchor repair.
The geometric starting point survives scrutiny:
\[ \boxed{\dim F\ge N/k,} \]
where \(N\) is the number of coordinates varying on an original face \(F\).
Indeed, edge directions span the face tangent.

The algorithm does not compute exact irrational spectral nullspaces.
Instead, compute rational approximations \(\widetilde g,\widetilde H\) to the potential gradient and Hessian, with
\[ \|\widetilde H-\nabla^2\Phi\|\le\eta/4. \]
Let \(Z\) be a rational basis for the exact face, cost, large-row, and protected-barrier constraints, additionally imposing
\[ \widetilde g^\top h=0. \]
Exact rational symmetric elimination finds a negative direction of
\[ \boxed{ Z^\top(\widetilde H+\eta I)Z. } \]
The identity shift is applied before restricting to the possibly poorly conditioned basis \(Z\). It converts the existence argument into a rational witness with a quantitative physical-coordinate curvature guarantee.
